item.title: Cloudflare launches Search for Agents to enable AI-powered site search
item.description:
Cloudflare launches Search for Agents to enable AI-powered site search

Cloudflare today introduced Search for Agents, a new toggle in the Cloudflare dashboard that creates an AI Search instance for a zone, indexes its content, and makes the search API available from the customer’s own domain.

🔍 Overview

  • Search for Agents is activated via a toggle in the Cloudflare dashboard.
  • It is available to all customers, including the Free plan (with limits).
  • Enabling the feature causes Cloudflare to create an AI Search instance, start indexing the zone’s content, and expose a searchable endpoint under the customer’s domain.

🧩 How it works

  • The feature can be turned on from the Quick Actions section of the zone page or via the API.
  • Once enabled, Cloudflare automatically creates the AI Search instance with default settings and begins crawling the site.
  • The search endpoint is advertised on every page of the site to facilitate discoverability.
  • If Markdown for Agents is also enabled, a request with Accept: text/markdown returns the same information in YAML front‑matter, allowing agents to pick up instructions easily.
  • Depending on the AI Search configuration, agents may query the endpoint using natural‑language questions.

⚙️ Configuration

  • The default AI Search instance can be re‑configured at any time, such as enabling reranking or changing cache settings.
  • Search usage is subject to the zone’s domain settings, including bot‑management rules, AI Crawl Control, and Web Application Firewall configurations.

🚀 Availability

  • Search for Agents can be enabled through the dashboard toggle or programmatically via the API.
  • The feature is offered to all customers, including those on the Free tier, though the Free tier operates under unspecified limits.

💡 Benefits

  • Provides a network‑level AI search API that any agent can discover and use without manual index setup.
  • Keeps search functionality under the customer’s own domain, preserving control over security and traffic policies.
  • Reduces operational overhead by automatically handling crawling, indexing, and endpoint advertisement.

#Cloudflare #SearchForAgents #AIsearch

Source: Introducing Search for Agents

item.title: Google ties Gemini AI to Search for schools, prompting backlash from officials
item.description:
Google ties Gemini AI to Search for schools, prompting backlash from officials

Google announced that starting next year, schools will not be able to disable Gemini-powered AI features without also losing access to Google Search, a change that has drawn sharp criticism from elected officials and major school districts.

🔍 Overview

  • Google vice president of education Chris Phillips told The New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” and schools turning off AI features “will not have access to Search.”
  • The policy shift means Gemini app, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be off by default until schools decide which services to enable, but they cannot keep Search while disabling the AI components.
  • New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders labeled the move “extortion.”
  • Both New York City and Chicago public schools have threatened to seek alternative search providers if Google does not offer a version of Search without AI.

⚙️ Key details

Google’s stated changes

  • Piloting “Guided Learning capabilities in Search” this month to walk students step-by-step through complex problems instead of giving quick answers.
  • Updating controls next year so Gemini app, Gemini Notebook, and Search are off by default until schools choose which to enable.
  • Building experiences “in partnership with educators” and listening to ensure products support students and teachers.

School district responses

District Response
New York City Public Schools Chancellor Kamar H. Samuels: “If Google doesn’t reconsider their position, we will explore other search options.”
Chicago Public Schools Told Google that if it cannot provide Search without AI, “the district will look to other search solutions.”

🏫 Political and educator concerns

  • Mayor Mamdani recently announced a policy barring 2-K-8 students from using AI in the classroom.
  • Educators worry about AI’s effect on students’ critical thinking skills; some studies show students who use AI generally perform worse on tests.
  • Concerns raised about mental health effects of children developing relationships with chatbots at a young age.
  • Google spokesperson Laura Breen stated: “We hear parents and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to shortcut learning, and we share the same goal: help students learn.”

💡 Why it matters

  • Google is deeply embedded in U.S. classrooms through Google Classroom, Chromebooks, and other services, making a fully Google-free transition difficult for districts.
  • The integration of AI into core search functionality removes the ability for schools to opt out of AI while retaining essential search tools.
  • The standoff highlights growing tension between AI deployment in education and pedagogical concerns about critical thinking and student wellbeing.

#Google #AI #Education #Search #Gemini #Policy

Source: The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search

item.title: Go client released for Qdrant vector search engine
item.description:
Go client released for Qdrant vector search engine

The Go client for the Qdrant vector search engine has been released, making it easier for developers to integrate vector search capabilities into their Go applications. Internally, the high-level client uses a low-level gRPC client to interact with Qdrant, abstracting away the complexity of direct API calls. The client supports secure communication with TLS 1.3 as the minimum required version when UseTLS is enabled.

📦 Availability

The client can be installed using the Go package manager:

  • go get -u github.com/qdrant/go-client

🔐 Security

  • Uses TLS 1.3 as the minimum security version when UseTLS: true is set

🧩 Architecture

  • High-level client provides simplified API for common operations
  • Low-level gRPC client handles direct communication with Qdrant server

💡 Why it matters

This release enables Go developers to leverage Qdrant’s vector search capabilities without implementing low-level networking code, accelerating the development of AI and machine learning applications that require semantic search functionality.

#Go #Qdrant #VectorSearch #gRPC #TLS #AI

Source: qdrant/go-client

item.title: NornicDB combines graph and vector search with sub-millisecond latency
item.description:
NornicDB combines graph and vector search with sub-millisecond latency

🔍 Overview

NornicDB is a distributed, low-latency database that integrates Graph and Vector capabilities with Temporal MVCC. It is designed to provide sub-millisecond performance for HNSW search, graph traversal, and writes.

🧩 How it works

The system allows users to query connected data using Cypher with compatible Bolt drivers. It supports combining graph traversal with vector and full-text retrieval. Historical state can be modeled using MVCC and retained history.

⚙️ Key details

  • Interfaces: Supports Neo4j Bolt/Cypher and qdrant’s gRPC, allowing switching without changes.
  • Features: Includes schemas, managed embeddings, reranking, LLM integration, GPU acceleration, Auto-TLP, Policy-based Memory Decay, and an MCP server.
  • Architecture: Multi-arch support includes CPU, CUDA, Metal, and Vulkan.
  • Integration: Can be embedded in Go applications and supports HTTP interfaces.

🚀 Availability

NornicDB is available via Docker images and native installers.

Platform Instructions
NVIDIA CUDA Use image timothyswt/nornicdb-amd64-cuda-bge:latest
Vulkan Use image timothyswt/nornicdb-amd64-vulkan-bge:latest
macOS Docker does not expose Metal acceleration; native install or local build required for GPU acceleration. Download .pkg installer (arm64 for Apple Silicon, amd64 for Intel) or use Homebrew.
Windows Run .\bin\nornicdb.exe serve

Users can access the admin UI at http://localhost:7474. Benchmark results depend on workload and hardware.

#GraphDatabase #VectorSearch #Cypher #NornicDB #GoLang

Source: orneryd/NornicDB

item.title: Simplifying Book Discovery with ML-Powered Visual Autocomplete Suggestions
item.description:
📚 Simplifying Book Discovery with ML-Powered Visual Autocomplete Suggestions

![Audible Visual Autocomplete Demo](https://assets.amazon.science/dims4/default/772c5bc/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1200x675+0+0/resize/900x506!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Famazon-topics-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fscien ce%2F12%2F70%2Fff2f2fdf400592ef6fd184390007%2Faudible-visualautocomplete-16x9.gif) Audible’s visual-autocomplete experience in action

Every day, millions of customers search for books across Amazon and Audible platforms. Traditional keyword autocomplete suggestions, while helpful, typically require multiple steps before customers find their desired content. To address this challenge, Amazon and Audible developed an innovative ML-powered visual autocomplete system that transforms the book discovery experience.

🎯 The Challenge: Streamlining Book Discovery

Traditional search experiences often involve several friction points:

  • Multiple steps from search query to purchase
  • Limited visual context in autocomplete suggestions
  • Generic recommendations without personalization
  • Separate navigation through search result pages

The goal was to create a more intuitive, personalized search experience that reduces the steps to purchase while handling millions of daily queries at scale.

🚀 The Solution: Instant Visual Autocomplete

The team developed an advanced visual autocomplete system that delivers immediate value to users:

✨ Key Features

  • Visual Previews: Book covers displayed instantly as users type
  • Direct Navigation: Skip search results pages entirely
  • Real-time Personalization: Format recommendations based on user preferences
  • Multi-entity Search: Access to book pages, author pages, and series pages
  • Low Latency: Optimized for millions of concurrent queries

🧠 Technical Architecture: Two Distinct Approaches

Audible’s Deep Pairwise Learning-to-Rank (DeepPLTR) Model

For Audible’s platform, the team implemented a sophisticated three-tower architecture:

![DeepPLTR Training Architecture](https://assets.amazon.science/dims4/default/212833b/2147483647/strip/true/crop/143 0x678+0+0/resize/1200x569!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Famazon-topics-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.co m%2Fscience%2F99%2F24%2F613646044b649bcdb459edad762d%2Ftraining-architecture-deeppltr.png) Training architecture of the DeepPLTR model

🏗️ Architecture Component

Tower Function Technology
Left Tower Contextual features and search patterns Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
Middle Tower Keyword and engagement history Historical interaction processing
Right Tower Customer preferences and personalization Product description analysis

The DeepPLTR model learns from paired examples during training but generates absolute scores at runtime for efficient ranking.

Amazon’s Two-Stage Modeling Approach

For Amazon’s broader catalog, the team chose a different strategy:

  1. Stage 1: Probabilistic information-retrieval model for title matching
  2. Stage 2: Personalization model for format recommendations (audiobooks, e-books, physical books)

This dual approach maintains ultra-low latency while enabling sophisticated personalization across Amazon’s massive inventory.

🔍 How It Works: From Keystrokes to Recommendations

Smart Intent Detection

The system employs advanced algorithms to understand user intent from minimal input:

  • Historical Data Analysis: Matches keystrokes to products using search history
  • Confidence Filtering: Distinguishes between general queries (“mystery”) and specific searches
  • Time-Decay Functions: Prioritizes recent user interactions

Real-World Example

When a customer types “dungeon craw”:

  1. System instantly recognizes intent for “Dungeon Crawler Carl” 2. Displays book cover and relevant metadata
  2. Provides direct navigation to product page 4. Shows related content (author page, series information)
  3. Personalizes format recommendations based on user history

📊 Impact and Benefits

For Customers ✅

  • Reduced Friction: Direct navigation eliminates search result pages
  • Visual Context: Book covers provide immediate recognition
  • Personalized Experience: Format recommendations match preferences
  • Enhanced Discovery: Access to authors and series information

For Business 💼

  • Increased Conversions: Fewer steps to purchase
  • Scale Performance: Handles millions of queries efficiently
  • Customer Satisfaction: More intuitive search experience
  • Data Insights: Rich interaction data for further optimization

🔬 Technical Innovation Highlights

Machine Learning Advances

  • Deep Learning Architecture: Multi-tower neural networks
  • Pairwise Learning: Advanced ranking algorithms
  • Real-time Processing: Sub-second response times
  • Personalization Engine: Individual user preference modeling

System Engineering

  • Scalable Infrastructure: Cloud-native architecture
  • Low Latency Design: Optimized for real-time interactions
  • Confidence Scoring: Quality assurance mechanisms
  • Multi-platform Deployment: Amazon and Audible integration

🌟 Future Implications

This technology represents more than improved book discovery—it’s establishing the foundation for next-generation search personalization across Amazon’s entire ecosystem. The innovations in visual autocomplete, intent detection, and real-time personalization have applications far beyond books.

🙌 Credits

Originally posted at: https://www.amazon.science/blog/simplifying-book-discovery-with-ml-powered-visual-autocomplete-suggestions

🏁 Conclusion

Amazon and Audible’s ML-powered visual autocomplete represents a significant leap forward in e-commerce search technology. By combining sophisticated machine learning models with intuitive user interfaces, the system successfully reduces friction in the book discovery process while maintaining the performance required for millions of daily users.

The dual approach—DeepPLTR for Audible and two-stage modeling for Amazon—demonstrates how technical solutions can be tailored to specific platform requirements while sharing core innovations. This work showcases the power of applied machine learning in solving real-world customer problems at scale.

Key takeaways include the importance of visual context in search, the value of personalization in recommendation systems, and the critical role of low-latency processing in user experience. These innovations lay the groundwork for future advances in search personalization and visual discovery across digital platforms.

item.title: 🔍 Context is King: How Contextual Document Embeddings Revolutionize Search Accuracy
item.description:
🔍 Context is King: How Contextual Document Embeddings Revolutionize Search Accuracy

Summary: Discover how traditional document embedding methods fall short by embedding passages in isolation, missing crucial context. Learn about InSeNT and Late Chunking, two groundbreaking techniques that significantly improve search accuracy by preserving document-wide context without increasing inference costs.

🌟 The Missing Piece in Modern Search

We’ve all been there – searching through a technical manual or scientific paper and getting frustratingly irrelevant results. Despite advances in search technology, why do our search engines still struggle to understand what we’re actually looking for?

The answer lies in 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝘅𝘁 – or rather, the lack of it. 🧩

Most modern search systems share a critical limitation: they break documents into smaller chunks before embedding them, effectively asking models to understand each passage in isolation. This approach fundamentally limits what search can accomplish, especially when the answer requires understanding information spread across multiple sections.

Think about it: how can a model properly interpret “They extended their dominance” without knowing whether we’re discussing Napoleonic armies or Brazilian football? 🤔

🔄 The Chunking Dilemma

Before we dive into solutions, let’s understand why search systems chunk documents in the first place:

  1. 📏 Fixed-length sliding windows (128-1024 tokens) are simple but create significant overlap
  2. 📑 Structure-aware blocks preserve semantic units but create variable lengths
  3. 🔄 Hybrid approaches attempt to balance structure with consistency

These chunking strategies reflect difficult trade-offs between respecting transformer model limits, preserving enough context for comprehension, and minimizing index bloat and latency.

The unfortunate reality? No chunking scheme can guarantee that all the evidence needed to answer a question will always be contained within a single chunk.

🚀 Introducing ConTEB, InSeNT, and Late Chunking

To address this challenge, researchers have developed two complementary innovations:

📊 ConTEB: Benchmarking Context Awareness

The Contextual Text Embedding Benchmark (ConTEB) introduces eight retrieval tasks specifically designed to penalize “context blindness.” These tasks range from synthetic datasets (Football, Geography) to realistic RAG workloads derived from NarrativeQA and Covid-QA.

The results confirm our suspicions: standard retrieval methods struggle significantly when context is key!

🔮 Late Chunking: A Paradigm Shift

Traditional embedding approaches use “early chunking,” where documents are first split into chunks, then each chunk is independently embedded:

1

φ(d) = [φ(c₁), φ(c₂), ..., φ(cₙ)]

Late Chunking flips this process on its head with a brilliantly simple approach:

  1. 🔄 One long forward pass - Concatenate all chunks into a single sequence, allowing tokens to attend to the entire document context
  2. 🧩 Recover chunk vectors afterward - For each original chunk, pool its token embeddings from the contextualized representation

This method maintains the same output shape expected by retrieval systems but now each chunk vector benefits from full-document context. Every token can influence the representation of every other token, capturing critical long-range dependencies.

💡 InSeNT: In-Sequence Negative Training

While Late Chunking alone shows impressive gains (+9.0 nDCG points on ConTEB), the researchers discovered that fine-tuning with a special technique called InSeNT (In-Sequence Negative Training) drives even greater improvements.

InSeNT uses two types of negatives during contrastive training:

  • Traditional in-batch negatives (chunks from different documents)
  • Novel in-sequence negatives (other chunks from the same document)

This balancing act achieves two complementary goals:

  • Training with different-document chunks encourages information propagation within documents
  • Training with same-document chunks ensures each chunk maintains its specificity

A small mixing weight (λ ≈ 0.1) helps balance these somewhat contradictory objectives.

📈 The Results Are In: Context Is Gold!

The experimental results are stunning:

  • Late Chunking alone delivers a +9.0 nDCG improvement
  • Adding InSeNT pushes the gain to +23.6 nDCG@10 compared to standard methods! 🎯

Not only that, but contextualized embeddings show additional benefits:

  • Better scaling with corpus size
  • Greater robustness to sub-optimal chunking strategies
  • Improved performance in ambiguous contexts

One interesting finding: Late Interaction models (ColBERT-style) actually perform worse with out-of-the-box Late Chunking (-0.3 nDCG@10). The researchers theorize that since these models learn without pooling, they develop very local features that don’t naturally leverage neighboring context. However, once trained with InSeNT, these models show dramatic improvements (+11.5 nDCG@10), suggesting that training is essential for context integration in these architectures.

🤔 Why This Matters

This research fundamentally changes how we should think about document embedding. Rather than seeing each chunk in isolation, we need systems that understand the relationship between chunks within the same document.

The promise of these techniques extends far beyond standard text retrieval. The researchers note that this approach could significantly improve visual retrievers like ColPali that currently embed single pages without broader document context.

And perhaps most importantly, these improvements come with minimal runtime overhead – a rare win-win in the world of information retrieval.

As the research aptly puts it: Context truly is gold when it comes to finding the gold passage. ✨

What context-aware search applications are you most excited to see improved with these techniques?
